report:
The entire partial argument is sound in its disclosed finite-PA operator domains and active-coefficient strictness convention. This verifies the scoped obstruction and the separate literal nonregularity result. It does not solve the original P05.2 classification; candidate=false remains appropriate.

I retrieved the literal [BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1) PDF and HTML and read the pertinent definitions and complete normal-invariance, refinement, PA/PC, factorial, and U(3,4) example proof units. The author ledger was not treated as verification. No full operator-extension theorem, real regularization theorem, toric comparison, or automatic continuity theorem for arbitrary competitors is needed here. The external premises below are source definitions and conventions.

The lattice geometry checks directly. Any three e_i have determinant ±1, so each coarse plane has saturated basis (e_i,e_j), and each fine cone has saturated basis (e_i,e_ij). The specified inward normals are primitive quotient generators. Their sums are −e_i at singleton rays and e_ij at pair rays, proving weight-one balancing. The quotient Z⁴/Z(1,1,1,1) has exactly the stated lattice identification. Normalizing the minimum coordinate to zero identifies X with the circuit-minimum support of U(3,4); its singleton–pair flat flags give exactly twelve fine cones. Singleton transverse germs have the unique three-ray relation, while nonzero pair-ray germs are complete planes. Thus the claimed concrete matroidal and lattice properties are established without assuming a stronger smoothness theorem.

The local-support proof is valid: a positive maximum above a segment chord forces the supporting slope to vanish, making the maximum set both open and closed. Segment convexity then propagates a support to each PCC endpoint, and barycentric summation proves Jensen. For PA functions, a support agrees with the tangential derivative along the tested face; balancing cancels that derivative and leaves nonnegative inward slacks. This proves positivity against every nonnegative balanced local cycle, rather than merely against [X]. Plane supports extend to ambient affine forms because their plane tangent lattices are saturated and, away from singleton rays and zero, sufficiently small neighborhoods lie entirely in that plane.

The PA/PC category identification also withstands independent checking. Positive local one-cycle tests enforce convexity along rational segments. At a rational PCC center, rational feasible barycentric coefficients give a balanced local ray cycle, whose nonnegative divisor bounds the initial directional slopes; segment convexity gives Jensen at the endpoints. Rational feasible coefficients are dense, and continuity of a PA function covers irrational centers. Conversely, for a nonnegative balanced k-cycle, choose a rational point in the tested face and subtract the same rational tangential correction from its inward normals so their weighted sum vanishes. Nearby rational endpoints then give the divisor inequality directly by Jensen. This avoids relying on source proof shortcuts involving subdivision at arbitrary irrational points.

All shared-face values agree: h and η restrict to the singleton coordinate r, while uε equals ε there and at zero. The displayed supports establish PC for η and P at zero, singleton rays, pair rays, interiors, and new bent edges. For Γ, singleton support slack is B/3, exceptional pair bend is 2A+B, other pair bend is S=A+B, and the origin support is strict because Γ≥Bh>0 off zero. These prove exactly the declared active-coefficient strictness. They do not prove the source's literal zero-coefficient wording, whose disclosed degeneracy is real. Conicality and Γ≥Bh establish positive recession slopes for every allowed parameter tuple.

The finite rational subdivision is genuine. Each exceptional half-cone is split at min(a,b)=ε; its lower region is a segment plus a singleton recession ray, and its upper region is a translated fine cone. There are sixteen top cells and exactly three vertices. The cut location remains rational for arbitrary real A,B,C because B cancels from the equality determining the cut. Integral parameters give integral tangent slopes and rational constants. Since P−Γ=Buε is bounded, P is a valid competitor and already regularizable through a constant sequence, or P+1/k. No pair-level regularity antecedent is being inferred from this endpoint.

Envelope maximality covers every source competitor. The opposite rational exceptional endpoints force q(0)≤Bε. Radial PCCs with arbitrarily distant rational endpoints give the stated singleton and nonexceptional pair-ray bounds; the exceptional ray bounds follow from the finite segment and obstacle itself. The θ-combinations lie in the relevant closed fine half-cones and are valid rational-endpoint PCCs. Their limits give exactly P on every rational point. For an irrational center, its relative rational face admits arbitrarily small rational simplices containing it. Cutting the complex by their rational facet hyperplanes gives a legitimate finite rational subdivision. Applying Jensen to their rational vertices and continuity only of P proves q≤P. No continuity of q is assumed. The same argument validates the irrational-center step for Q_n.

Constants cancel from both divisor stages. At zero, P has germ Bε+Sη, producing singleton weights zero, exceptional weights 2S, and other pair weights S; these balance and give mass 4S². At either special vertex, the four primitive directions have weights (2A+B,2S,B,B) and outgoing slopes (B,0,S,S). Their weighted vector sum is zero, and their second divisor is B(4A+3B). The global first cycle has precisely these vertex balances; its remaining edges are straight with constant weights. Since the carrying structure has only three vertices, there are no additional atoms. Refinement inserts cancelling contributions inside affine cells and at subdivisions of affine cycle edges, preserving the actual finite operator without lattice indices or an extra factorial.

At each special vertex, the four active gradients have convex hull of area B(4A+3B)/2. Supporting inequalities give inclusion in the subdifferential, and a separating direction excludes every point outside that hull. Thus the directly computed raw atom is twice the Alexandrov area at these complete plane germs. No ambient volume is used at the singular origin. The reference first weights are B, 2A+B, and S in the stated positions; they balance and give degree 4A²+16AB+10B². The endpoint has exactly the same total mass. Its gap is (B−C)uε, nonzero at the origin and zero at both other atoms, so the contact integral is exactly −4(C−B)ε(A+B)²<0.

The literal nonregularity proposition is correct for every n≥2. The obstacle v_n is continuous, bounded, and literal PA on rational level cuts. Q_n is an ambient-convex competitor, and the radial rational PCC bounds establish its exact envelope. Every literal PAPC approximant has nondecreasing integral slopes on the primitive segment [0,e₁]; this also follows directly from local one-cycle positivity. Its right midpoint slope is either ≥1 or ≤0. Comparing the corresponding half-segment increment with slope 1−1/n gives uniform error at least 1/(4n). Consequently Q_n has no literal uniform regularization. No regularizable MA is assigned to it.

Two harmless wording clarifications should be explicit. The intersection clause of the local-support lemma concerns PA f on a common carrying structure; its segment and Jensen clauses concern continuous f. Also, span(σ) is valid for conical cells only: translated cells require span(σ−σ), as the manuscript's main convention already states. Every actual application satisfies these domains, and neither clarification changes a proof or measured endpoint.

All four numerical rows, polygon areas, and grid-count totals independently check: 1,014 point checks and 1,800 midpoint checks per tuple, hence 4,056 and 7,200 overall. These remain finite evidence. The primary retrieval metadata matches the reported version, dates, page count, and extracted-line count. Historical execution, compilation, environment, and retained-file hash claims cannot be authenticated from the supplied text alone; they are not mathematical premises and are not used for this verdict. No operational rerun or settings change was performed.

The exact proved scope is a family of strictly supported, positive-growth references on this particular saturated U(3,4) fan with genuine PA envelopes violating contact, plus literal nonregularity for h. The simplest literal pair therefore lies outside the source's pair-level regularity antecedent, while its main chosen endpoint still has a valid literal raw measure and negative contact integral. In the declared real category, any universal regularized contact theory agreeing with the finite formula cannot hold together with all-obstacle regularity on these pairs. All-obstacle real regularity, stronger unspecified smoothness packages, and necessary-and-sufficient conditions for general balanced pairs remain unproved. The unchanged original classification gap remains open.

passages.statement: BMPSv1 uses Nσ=N∩span_R(σ−σ) and inward primitive generators of Nσ/Nτ. For PA f and balanced rational c∈Z_k(Π), (f·c)(τ)=Σσ≻τc(σ)fσ(nσ/τ)−fτ(Σσ≻τc(σ)nσ/τ), for τ∈Π^(k−1).
BMPSv1 PA consists of continuous functions affine on a finite rational structure, with integral tangent slopes and rational constants.

BMPSv1 PCCs have xi∈X∩N_Q, real αi∈[0,1], Σαi=1, x=Σαixi, and x∈τ, xi∈σi, τ⪯σi on some rational structure. PC requires every PCC Jensen inequality; PAPC requires f·c≥0 for every k, open U⊂X, and nonnegative balanced c∈Z_k(U).
BMPSv1 strictness on Π requires strict Jensen for PCCs with x∈relint(τ), xi∈relint(σi), and τ≺σi for two distinct indices; zero coefficients are allowed.
BMPSv1 PCreg(X,γ) consists of continuous uniform decreasing PAPC(X,γ) limits; PAPC(X,γ) requires bounded difference from γ.
BMPSv1 defines Pγ(u)=sup{q≤γ+u:q∈PC(X),q≤γ+O(1)} for continuous u and PAPC γ positive at infinity. Positivity means γσ(v)>0 for every face σ and 0≠v∈rec(σ).

BMPSv1 defines MApoly(f)=Σv(f^d·[X])(v)δv and deg(f)=MApoly(f)(X) for PA f on balanced pure d-dimensional X. Its Alexandrov measure is dual-lattice-normalized subgradient volume for convex functions on open affine lattice domains.

BMPSv1 orthogonality assumes pair-level regularity and requires ∫(Pγ(u)−γ−u)MApoly(Pγ(u))=0 for every bounded literal PA obstacle u.
